source_title: WHO urban health and city air-quality guidance
unit_or_scope: urban populations and city monitoring systems
direct_observation: polluted urban air is widespread; transport systems create air and noise pollution; cities need measurement and reporting
missing_stage: named source-to-person exposure symptom care and remedy
next_test: pair official stations and local sensors with named schools workplaces routes and health records

unit_or_scope: deprived populations near traffic and industry
direct_observation: ambient exposure inequalities are associated with deprived areas and limited capacity to relocate or access care
missing_stage: named subgroup exposure dose health and protection after intervention
next_test: compare source proximity mobility constraints and health outcomes by subgroup

unit_or_scope: EU regions and local pollution-health atlas
direct_observation: PM2.5 improved in rich and poor regions but remained around one-third higher in poorer regions; regional proxy limits causal inference
missing_stage: neighbourhood hotspot exposure displacement and direct health effect
next_test: link NUTS3 trends to local hotspot and socioeconomic microdata

unit_or_scope: European local pollution and health indicators
direct_observation: maps PM2.5 NO2 ozone exposure and health indicators at the most disaggregated available level but is not itself a causal tool
next_test: audit whether mapped hotspots receive enforcement and exposure reduction

source_title: World Bank global air-pollution data work
unit_or_scope: more than 32000 cities and global sources
direct_observation: transport industry power and biomass burning drive health damage and economic loss; global estimates do not identify local policy effects
missing_stage: named intervention effects on exposure health mobility cost jobs and justice
next_test: follow one corridor or facility through source control exposure and household outcomes

unit_or_scope: London roads and communities compared with modeled no-ULEZ scenario in 2024
direct_observation: Estimated roadside NO2 was 27 percent lower across London 24 percent lower in outer London and 54 percent lower in central London than without all ULEZ expansions; some deprived communities near busy roads saw an estimated 80 percent reduction in people exposed to illegal levels and vehicle compliance reached 97 percent
missing_stage: person-level dose health mobility cost traffic displacement school and worker continuity enforcement burden and remedy
evidence_status: official TfL/London report; modeled counterfactual and aggregate exposure estimates not individual health outcomes
next_test: link monitoring locations and deprived corridors to measured dose health attendance travel cost and adjacent-area exposure

source_title: Mayor of London Annual Report 2024-25 school air-filter programme
unit_or_scope: 200 primary schools in London prioritized by poorer air quality and higher deprivation
direct_observation: London invested 2.7 million pounds in indoor air-quality filters for every classroom in 200 primary schools
closed_stage: targeted indoor-protection delivery and environmental-justice operation
missing_stage: measured classroom PM2.5 filter use maintenance symptoms attendance learning and child-level health
evidence_status: official mayoral annual report; provision and targeting reported without public outcome follow-up
next_test: follow selected schools through indoor measurements filter uptime symptoms attendance and maintenance by deprivation and proximity to traffic

source_title: Imperial and City Hall Health burden of air pollution in London in 2024
unit_or_scope: Greater London population and modeled pollution-mortality burden in 2019 and 2024
direct_observation: Updated modeling estimates premature deaths attributable to air pollution fell from approximately 6400-8000 in 2019 to 3800-5100 in 2024 with an estimated 3.8-5.1 billion pound economic cost
missing_stage: ULEZ-specific attribution individual exposure dose health records subgroup equity and remedy
evidence_status: official City Hall and Imperial assessment; scenario-based burden estimate explicitly not attribution to ULEZ or one policy
next_test: disaggregate mortality and admissions by borough deprivation age and source while separating ULEZ effects from other policies and secular trends

source_title: London-wide ULEZ six-month report schools and child asthma
unit_or_scope: 1752 schools and educational establishments with about 880000 attendees inside expanded ULEZ plus London children under 19
direct_observation: Report identifies 2705 emergency asthma admissions among London children under 19 in 2022/23 and higher pollution exposure among deprived and Black Asian and Minority Ethnic communities; expanded ULEZ included 1752 schools
closed_stage: place-based school exposure and child-health burden fields
missing_stage: individual before-after exposure admissions attendance symptoms learning and causal ULEZ effect
evidence_status: official London report; population health and exposure context without same-child follow-up
next_test: link schools and child health records to measured exposure admissions attendance and deprivation before and after intervention
